commands.author: mushuiyu886

target.title: fix(acp): reject malformed session list cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP clients and bundled Pi/OpenCode session catalog callers could send a malformed opaque pagination cursor and receive a plausible session or transcript page instead of an invalid-cursor error.

Node's base64url decoder ignores some invalid characters and accepts non-canonical padding. The ACP and plugin input paths also trimmed cursor strings before decoding. Because the original token was not checked exactly, values that OpenClaw never emitted could still reach Gateway, Pi session-store, or OpenCode CLI pagination.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each owning path now preserves the original opaque cursor and verifies that decoded bytes round-trip to the exact unpadded base64url token before parsing JSON or using the offset. This follows the existing strict encoded-request pattern in OpenClaw while keeping ACP and plugin ownership separate.

Valid cursors and the encoded cursor format are unchanged. This does not change schemas, limits, storage, or the Anthropic catalog path; the latter has separate open cursor-validation work in #104967.

## User Impact

Malformed ACP, Pi, and OpenCode catalog cursors now fail clearly instead of silently returning misleading pagination results. Cursors returned by OpenClaw continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Malformed session pagination cursors containing ignored characters, non-canonical padding, or surrounding whitespace were accepted as valid.

**Environment tested:** Linux, Node 24.15.0, pinned OpenClaw main reproduction plus the patched local Gateway, real WebSocket transport, real `openclaw acp` subprocess, and ACP stdio JSON-RPC frames.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Started the patched Gateway, spawned `node openclaw.mjs acp --url ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --token-file <file>`, sent ACP `initialize`, then sent `session/list` with no cursor, a canonical cursor, the same cursor with an appended `$`, and the canonical cursor wrapped in spaces.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
initialize: protocolVersion=1 listCapability=true
omittedCursor: accepted=true sessions_count=1 nextCursor=null
canonicalCursorControl: accepted=true sessions_count=1 nextCursor=null
malformedCursor: rejected=true
error.code=-32603
error.data.details=Invalid ACP session list cursor.
whitespaceWrappedCursor: rejected=true
error.data.details=Invalid ACP session list cursor.
gateway: sessions.list completed for the valid request path
```

Pinned-main before/after control:

```text
before (084d1d96374f4e10e0db577180c60fc57a66639e):
  omitted cursor accepted
  canonical cursor accepted
  canonical cursor + "$" also accepted and returned a normal page

after:
  omitted cursor accepted
  canonical cursor accepted
  canonical cursor + "$" rejected before pagination
  whitespace-wrapped canonical cursor rejected before pagination
```

Focused validation:

```text
ACP stable session-list handler: 1 file, 13 tests passed
ACP session-list helper: 1 file, 4 tests passed
Pi session catalog: 1 file, 17 tests passed
OpenCode session catalog: 1 file, 9 tests passed
targeted core lint: passed
targeted extension lint: passed
format check: 6 files passed
gatewayWatch runtime build: passed (tsdown, CLI bootstrap guard, runtime postbuild, stamps)
git diff --check: passed
```

The local changed-surface run completed core, core-test, extension, and extension-test typechecks before its full-repository lint shard was terminated with signal 143. The focused lint commands above then passed for every changed file.

**Observed result after fix:** Non-canonical cursors fail before Gateway/session-store/CLI pagination, including tokens with ignored characters or surrounding whitespace, while omitted and canonical controls still return normal pages.

**What was not tested:** No Crabbox/Testbox backend was available. A full declaration-producing `pnpm build` could not complete locally because `rolldown-plugin-dts` exhausted the available heap; the supported skip-dts `gatewayWatch` runtime build passed. No external provider or channel was needed for this ACP/session-catalog boundary.
